items.stem: What is the function of retina in the human eye?
items.answer: Retina acts as screen for the images formed by the eye lens.

items.stem: What is pupil?
items.answer: Pupil is a narrow hole through which light enters in eye and falls on eye lens.

items.stem: Name the cells responsible for colour perception.
items.answer: Cone cells are responsible for colour perception.

items.stem: Name the cells responsible for intensity of light.
items.answer: Rod cells present on retina are responsible for intensity of light.

items.stem: What is the function of ciliary muscles?
items.answer: Ciliary muscles can increase or decrease the focal length of eye lens to focus the images at retina.

items.stem: What do you mean by accommodation of eye?
items.answer: The ability of eye lens to adjust its focal length is called accommodation.

items.stem: What is blind spot?
items.answer: It is a part of retina where if the image of any object is formed, the sensation of formation of image is conveyed by optic nerves to the brain.
items.ocr: Printed question number was dropped by OCR; inferred as 38 from its position between questions 37 and 39.

items.stem: What is colour blindness?
items.answer: If some cone cells are absent from retina, the person is not able to distinguish the colours of the object. It is called colour blindness.

items.stem: Name the part of the human eye that helps in changing the focal length of the eye lens.
items.answer: Ciliary muscles.

items.stem: What is the role of pupil in a human eye?
items.answer: Pupil regulates and controls the amount of light entering the eye.
items.ocr: The book prints an OR-variant of the same question: "What is the function of pupil in human eye?" Kept the first phrasing as the stem.

items.stem: Name the part of the eye (a) that controls the amount of light entering into the eye. (b) that has real, inverted image of the object formed on it.
items.answer: (a) Pupil, (b) Retina.

items.stem: Write the value of near point of distinct vision for normal eye.
items.answer: 25 cm

items.stem: What is the range of vision of a normal human eye?
items.answer: 25 cm to infinity.

items.stem: Name the condition of eye in which the person cannot see near and far objects clearly.
items.answer: Presbyopia.

items.stem: What is the focal length of the eye lens?
items.answer: 25 cm in relaxed state.
items.ocr: Printed answer reads "25 cm in relaxed state" and is kept verbatim, but the accepted physical value for the relaxed eye lens is about 2.5 cm; the printed figure looks like a lost decimal point (or a confusion with the 25 cm near point). Flagged for reviewer, not silently altered.

items.stem: A man uses glasses of power 1 dioptre and cannot see clearly beyond 1 m. Name the defect of vision.
items.answer: Myopia.
items.ocr: Stem printed as "power 1 dioptre"; the minus sign appears to have been dropped, since a far point of 1 m needs a concave lens of −1 D. Kept the printed wording; the printed answer (myopia) is consistent with −1 D.

items.stem: A person is advised to wear spectacles with convex lenses. State the defect of vision he is suffering from.
items.answer: Hypermetropia.

items.stem: What is the angle between the two lateral faces of a prism called?
items.answer: The angle between the two lateral faces of a prism is called angle of the prism.

items.stem: Why refractive index of glass is different with respect to different colours of light?
items.answer: It is due to different velocities of components of light in glass.

items.stem: Which light ray has the maximum velocity in glass?
items.answer: Red.

items.stem: Which light ray has the minimum velocity in glass?
items.answer: Violet.

items.stem: Define dispersion.
items.answer: The splitting of white light into its seven constituent colours, if white light is passed through prism is called dispersion.

items.stem: What does VIBGYOR refer to?
items.answer: VIBGYOR refers to V = Violet, I = Indigo, B = Blue, G = Green, Y = Yellow, O = Orange and R = Red.
items.ocr: Answer was printed as LaTeX fragments ($V = {\mathrm{Violet}}$, $I =$ Indigo, ... $R = {\mathrm{Red}}$); rewritten into plain Unicode text.

items.stem: What is angle of dispersion?
items.answer: The angle between red light and violet light after dispersion by prism is called angle of dispersion.

items.stem: Which light is deviated more red or violet?
items.answer: Red light is deviated least and violet light is deviated more.

items.stem: Which coloured component bends the least during the dispersion of the white light through prism?
items.answer: Red.

items.stem: Name the optical phenomenon due to which stars twinkle.
items.answer: Atmospheric refraction of light.

items.stem: When a light ray passes obliquely through the atmosphere in an upward direction, how does its path generally change?
items.answer: The light ray will bend away from its normal direction.

items.stem: How would the sky appear in the absence of earth's atmosphere?
items.answer: Scattering by molecules of gases in atmosphere makes sky appear blue. In absence of atmosphere on earth, no scattering occurs. So, the sky appears black.

items.stem: Name the essential parts of human eye.
items.answer: (i) Cornea, (ii) Iris, (iii) Pupil, (iv) Eye lens, (v) Ciliary muscles, (vi) Retina.
items.ocr: Stripped the trailing page furniture "Click Here to Buy book on Flipkart" that followed this answer.

items.stem: Which liquid fills the space behind the cornea?
items.answer: Aqueous humour.

items.stem: Which part of the eye controls the amount of light entering the eye?
items.answer: The pupil.

items.stem: What is eye lens made of?
items.answer: It is made of a jelly like material.

items.stem: How is the sense of vision carried from the eye to the brain?
items.answer: Through the optic nerve.

items.stem: A person is advised to wear spectacles with concave lenses. What type of defect of vision is he suffering from?
items.answer: Myopia.

items.stem: What is meant by least distance of distinct vision?
items.answer: The minimum distance at which objects can be seen most distinctly without strain is called the least distance of distinct vision.

items.stem: What kind of lens is used in the spectacles of a person suffering from myopia?
items.answer: Concave lens.

items.stem: Name the component of eye that is responsible for the adjustment of eye lens.
items.answer: Ciliary muscles.

items.stem: A person suffering from an eye defect uses lenses of power 1 D. Name the defect he is suffering from and the nature of lens used.
items.answer: Defect – Hypermetropia. Nature of lens – Convex lens.
items.ocr: Stem printed as "power 1 D"; the plus sign appears lost in OCR, since the printed answer (hypermetropia, convex lens) requires +1 D. Kept the printed wording.

items.stem: Name the defect of vision in which eye-lens loses its power of accommodation due to old age.
items.answer: Presbyopia.

items.stem: Name the process which is involved in the formation of a rainbow.
items.answer: Dispersion of light.

items.stem: Atmospheric refraction causes advance sunrise and delayed sunset. By how much time is (a) Sunrise advanced? (b) Sunset delayed?
items.answer: (a) Sunrise is advanced by about 2 minutes. (b) Sunset is delayed by about 2 minutes.

items.stem: State one function of iris in human eye.
items.answer: It controls the size of the pupil.

items.stem: What is the nature of the image formed on the retina?
items.answer: Real, inverted and same-sized.

items.stem: What is meant by dispersion of light?
items.answer: The splitting of light into its component colours is called dispersion of light.

items.stem: Name the type of particles which acts as a prism in the formation of rainbow in the sky.
items.answer: Water droplets present in the atmosphere.

items.stem: Which coloured component bends the least during the dispersion of white light through prism?
items.answer: Red.
items.ocr: The book prints this question twice with different year tags (also as question 57, Foreign 2011); both are retained under their own printed numbers.

items.stem: The ciliary muscles of a normal eye are in their (i) most relaxed, (ii) most contracted state. In which of the two cases is the focal length of the eye lens more?
items.answer: The focal length of eye-lens is more when the ciliary muscles of a normal eye are in their most relaxed state.

items.stem: Name the outermost layer of the eye. What is its function?
items.answer: Sclerotic. It protects and holds the eye.
